title: Adaptive Learning Integration
definition: The process of integrating new knowledge into a model while minimizing the loss of old knowledge.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Imagine learning a new language. To avoid forgetting old words, you practice them alongside the new ones. Adaptive learning integration does something similar for AI models.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: Adaptive learning integration is a method that combines the principles of continual learning and Parameter Stability Loss to ensure that a model learns new tasks without forgetting old ones. This is achieved by merging updates carefully and scaling them down to prevent overwriting.
difficulty_levels.expert: Adaptive learning integration is a novel approach that addresses catastrophic forgetting in machine learning models. It applies techniques from continual learning, such as sequential model merging and Parameter Stability Loss, to maintain a balanced integration of knowledge. This approach has philosophical implications for the role of stability and balance in learning systems and connects to research in fields such as neuroscience and cognitive psychology.

extra_fields.insight: The insight that simultaneous, reduced-strength merging can help maintain a balanced integration of knowledge while mitigating catastrophic forgetting.
